text.p: The following are top headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Alberta, B.C. strong in math test: Canadian students trail Asians, edge Germans and Americans in international competition.
- Civil servants facing new cuts: Ontario to chop another $3-billion.
- Tobacco legislation hastily recalled: Crackdown leak stirred concern.
- 101 charged with sale of baby seal pelts: Ottawa probes record East Coast hunt.
- Athletes use protein to enhance training.
- Mandate in Africa muddied: Prepare mission for various duties, commanders told.
- U.S. firm bids for Altamira: Venture company TA eclipses Manulife offer by proposing $783-million for fund manager.
- Honda scouting for new plant: Setting sights on North America.
- Robert Friedland's diamond play in China collapses: Failure to reach agreement with shareholders nixes deal.
- Altamira draws big U.S. bid: Boston-based TA Associates offers to pay $6 a share more than Manulife for the mutual fund firm, but only if its conditions are met.
- Anvil Range shares fall 64 percent as mining suspended in Yukon.
